opening: Easy, {name}. Your body is newly woven, but your soul is older than this chamber.
Before the Memory Loom tells you how this life will begin, you must understand why the Well returned you at all.

I will show you seven memories: Old Earth's Age of Dust, the rise of Sartan and Patryn, the Sundering, Xar and Haplo, the four realm journey, the Seventh Gate, and the original SoulDrift that led to your return. Finish them, and then I will tell you what this soul has become.

raceLines.human: Human souls adapt by borrowing the shape of every realm they survive. Yours carries several incompatible echoes at once. That is why the Well chose you—and why ordinary gates can no longer keep you out.
raceLines.elf: Elven memory was meant to preserve a single unbroken thread. Yours contains a memory from before the Sundering, although no living Elf should possess it. You are here because the past is trying to remember itself through you.
raceLines.dwarf: Dwarven forge-clans anchored the realm locks with stone and bronze. When the western anchor failed, its missing keystone pattern burned itself into your soul. You are here because the broken machinery of creation recognizes you as one of its parts.
raceLines.halfling: Halfling wayfinders discovered paths the Architects never intended to leave open. You carried refugees along one of those hidden roads—and the road followed you back into the Well. You are here because every sealed realm now contains a path that remembers your feet.

callingLines.warrior: Your mortal weapon discipline can meet hostile realm pressure without immediately breaking. That gift will hurt before it saves anyone.
callingLines.mage: Your color channels can read the grammar shared by all realms. Do not mistake understanding a law for controlling it.
callingLines.priest: You can keep a soul coherent while realities argue over its shape. Many will need that mercy.
callingLines.sharpshooter: You see the lines along which a realm is about to move. The right shot can alter more than a battle.
callingLines.paladin: Your oaths create temporary law. In a collapsing world, a promise held long enough can become shelter.
callingLines.summoner: The shapes answering your commands are memories of creatures that might once have existed in the First World.
callingLines.asura: You hear the pressure beneath thought—the same black resonance the Architects tried to divide and bury. Use it without becoming its doorway.
callingLines.slayer: You recognize the weak seam in anything: armor, lies, even a realm boundary. Some seams must be cut; others must be guarded.
callingLines.shadowknight: A Fire-Realm ember keeps your half-dead soul from passing on. Steal only the life you need, or the hunger will decide what remains of you.

choices.label: Open the Chronicle of Returning.
choices.response: Pass through all seven boards once. You may advance past any individual narration immediately, and leaving only pauses your place. The final memory names the shared SoulDrifter task; only then will the Loom accept three stat threads, one ancestry boon, and one mortal base discipline.

choices.label: Why did the Well choose me?
choices.response: It did not choose one hero. It resurrected many souls capable of carrying contradictory laws. Finish the chronicle and you will see why your particular {race} {calling} pattern survived.

choices.label: Who were the Architects?
choices.response: The oldest chronicle names the Sartan who performed the Sundering and the Patryns they imprisoned. Our continuation names later builders Architects when the exact hand is unknown. The storybook keeps those histories separate.

choices.label: Tell me what to do first.
choices.response: First finish the chronicle and seal your starter imprint. Your worn clothing and mundane weapon are already equipped; the coffer holds the binding charm and recovery bands needed for the trial doors.

opening: The stones ahead belong to two different ruins. Watch the cyan seams: they mark where one set of physical laws gives way to another.

Choose how you want danger to move. Tactical Turns let you study every command. Real-Time keeps the same rules but lets the encounter flow continuously. Your character, skills, and rewards remain the same.

choices.label: Mark the safe route.
choices.response: I marked it, but routes drift. Trust the line only until the world gives you a reason not to.

choices.label: I understand.
choices.response: Then speak with Brannoc before crossing the arena line. He has buried enough students to dislike surprises.

opening: That construct is old, angry, and honest. It will show its attack line before it strikes. Use {defensiveSkill} when you need to survive an impact.
Your first technique is {signatureSkill}. At this level the pattern is small and the effect is brief. Skill and equipment will add stronger shapes later; for now, timing matters more than spectacle.

choices.label: Begin the Sentinel trial.
choices.response: Cross the cyan threshold when ready. Recover the Soul Essence after the construct falls—and do not let its memories convince you they are your own.
